# Facet Joint Injection Clinical Compass

## CPT Codes

| CPT | Description | RVU | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 64490 | Injection(s), diagnostic or therapeutic agent, paravertebral facet (zygapophyseal) joint (or nerves innervating that joint) with image guidance; cervical or thoracic, single level | 3.44 | Cervical/thoracic facet injection or MBB — single level |
| 64491 | Injection(s), diagnostic or therapeutic agent, paravertebral facet joint; cervical or thoracic, second level | 1.82 | Add-on code — second level |
| 64492 | Injection(s), diagnostic or therapeutic agent, paravertebral facet joint; cervical or thoracic, third and any additional level(s) | 1.62 | Add-on code — third+ level |
| 64493 | Injection(s), diagnostic or therapeutic agent, paravertebral facet joint; lumbar or sacral, single level | 3.28 | Lumbar/sacral facet injection or MBB — single level |
| 64494 | Injection(s), diagnostic or therapeutic agent, paravertebral facet joint; lumbar or sacral, second level | 1.72 | Add-on code — second level |
| 64495 | Injection(s), diagnostic or therapeutic agent, paravertebral facet joint; lumbar or sacral, third and any additional level(s) | 1.52 | Add-on code — third+ level |

## ICD-10 Codes

| ICD-10 | Description | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M54.5 | Low back pain | Primary code for lumbar facet syndrome |
| M47.816 | Spondylosis without myelopathy or radiculopathy, lumbar region | Lumbar facet arthropathy |
| M47.812 | Spondylosis without myelopathy or radiculopathy, cervical region | Cervical facet arthropathy |
| M54.2 | Cervicalgia | Cervical facet pain |
| M47.896 | Other spondylosis, lumbar region | Lumbar spondylosis |
| M54.59 | Other low back pain | Non-specific low back pain |

## Payer Requirements

Tabs: Medicare | Medicaid | Private Insurance

### Medicare

**Prior Authorization Requirements**
- Clinical diagnosis of facetogenic pain (axial pain, extension-provoked, no neurologic deficit)
- Documentation of conservative therapy failure: ≥3 months PT and analgesics
- Imaging (X-ray or MRI) showing facet arthropathy or spondylosis
- Physician attestation of medical necessity
- Frequency limit: 3 injections per region per year (Medicare LCD)
- For MBB: documentation of intent to proceed to RFA if positive response

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- ✓ Axial spine pain with extension/rotation provocation pattern
- ✓ Clinical pattern consistent with facetogenic pain (referred pain to buttock/groin/posterior thigh)
- ✓ Failed conservative therapy (PT, NSAIDs, analgesics) for ≥3 months
- ✓ No predominant radicular component

**Reimbursement:** Medicare covers facet injections and medial branch blocks under applicable LCD. Fluoroscopic guidance is included in the CPT code. Frequency limits apply — document each injection date and response.

**Known Payer Policies**

| Payer | Policy | Covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Medicare (CMS) | Covered per LCD; 3 injections/region/year; fluoroscopy included in CPT | Yes |

### Medicaid

**Prior Authorization Requirements**
- State-specific prior authorization required
- Clinical diagnosis documentation
- Conservative therapy failure documentation
- Physician attestation

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- ✓ Axial pain with facetogenic pattern
- ✓ Failed conservative therapy

**Reimbursement:** Medicaid coverage varies by state. Prior authorization typically required. Some states have strict frequency limits.

**Known Payer Policies**

| Payer | Policy | Covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Medicaid (state-specific) | Prior auth required; frequency limits vary by state | Yes |

### Private Insurance

**Prior Authorization Requirements**
- Prior authorization required by most commercial payers
- Clinical documentation of facetogenic pain pattern
- Imaging showing facet arthropathy
- Documentation of ≥3 months conservative therapy failure
- Frequency limit: typically 3 injections per region per year
- For MBB series: documentation of RFA plan if positive response

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- ✓ Axial spine pain with extension provocation and facetogenic referral pattern
- ✓ Imaging-confirmed facet arthropathy or spondylosis
- ✓ Failed conservative therapy (PT, NSAIDs) for ≥3 months

**Reimbursement:** Commercial payers typically cover facet injections and MBBs with prior authorization. Fluoroscopy is included in the CPT code. Some payers require step therapy (PT before injections).

**Known Payer Policies**

| Payer | Policy | Covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Aetna | Covered; requires 3-month PT failure and imaging correlation | Yes |
| UnitedHealthcare | Covered with prior auth; clinical documentation required | Yes |
| BCBS (most plans) | Covered; 3 injections/region/year; prior auth required | Yes |
| Cigna | Covered with prior auth; facetogenic pain pattern documentation required | Yes |
| Humana | Covered; prior auth and conservative therapy documentation required | Yes |

## Required Documentation

### Imaging
- X-ray or MRI showing facet arthropathy or spondylosis at symptomatic levels
- Absence of significant disc herniation or nerve root compression (to distinguish from radiculopathy)

### Clinical Documentation
- H&P documenting axial pain pattern, extension provocation, and referred pain distribution
- Pain scores at multiple visits (NRS or VAS)
- Functional impairment documentation
- Documentation of absence of predominant neurologic deficit

### Conservative Therapy
- PT notes documenting ≥3 months of lumbar/cervical stabilization and core strengthening
- NSAIDs or analgesics trial documentation
- Activity modification documentation

### Procedure Documentation
- Fluoroscopy confirmation of needle placement at facet joint or medial branch
- Volume and agent documentation (local anesthetic ± steroid)
- Post-procedure pain diary (for MBB — document % relief at 30 min and 2 hours)

## Submission Process

1. Establish clinical diagnosis of facetogenic pain (axial pain, extension-provoked, no neurologic deficit)
2. Obtain imaging showing facet arthropathy or spondylosis
3. Document conservative therapy failure (≥3 months PT and analgesics)
4. Submit prior authorization with CPT codes (64493 ± 64494 for lumbar), ICD-10 codes, and clinical documentation
5. Include imaging report, PT notes, and pain score documentation
6. For MBB: document intent to proceed to RFA if ≥80% relief achieved
7. Document post-procedure pain diary results for diagnostic blocks
8. If denied, request peer-to-peer review citing clinical pattern and PT failure

## Common Denial Reasons

- ⚠ Frequency limit exceeded (3/region/year) — document exceptional circumstances
- ⚠ Missing clinical documentation of facetogenic pain pattern (axial pain, extension provocation)
- ⚠ Imaging not confirming facet arthropathy — ensure X-ray or MRI shows facet changes
- ⚠ Insufficient conservative therapy documentation (document ≥3 months PT explicitly)
- ⚠ Wrong CPT code for level (cervical vs. lumbar) or add-on codes not used correctly
- ⚠ Prior authorization not obtained before procedure
- ⚠ Missing post-procedure pain diary for diagnostic MBB (required for RFA authorization)
